FHA Solutions Inc. is growing, and we're looking for an experienced telecom professional to join our Operations team as a Project Manager. This role is fully remote, with flexible hours built around getting the job done.

Projects remain on schedule and issues are identified and addressed early

Project information, financials, and tracking systems remain accurate and up to date

We pay the highest rates in the industry, and offer the strongest annual increases in the sector. On top of that, you'll get:
A competitive bonus structure based purely on individual performance
Flexible hours built around getting the job done

70% of our portfolio is LLM-powered. You’ll scope AI features, plan around model risk, and use Cursor and Claude yourself to write specs and plans faster.

Not every environment fits everyone, so here’s an honest picture of the teammate we’re looking for.
You’ll thrive here if:
You own the outcome: scope, timeline, quality, and the relationship.
You’re technical enough that engineers can’t hand-wave you, and clear enough that founders never feel lost.
You can tell a founder no, with a reason and a plan.
You wear many hats without being asked: PM today, BA tomorrow, QA on release day.
You step into an at-risk project and bring it back to green.

Wear whatever hat the project needs to win.

3+ years running software delivery at an agency, consulting firm, or startup. That means you owned the projects, not just attended the standups.

Sr. Project Manager - Environmental Remediation, Byram Township, NJ Posted:

Summary Of Job Description

The Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) assists CAPE in achieving strategic and business objectives by leading project management processes (initiation, planning, executing, monitoring/controlling, and closing) for projects across New Jersey. This Sr. PM role is responsible for both construction and environmental remediation delivery and must be capable of managing field execution, subcontractors, schedules, budgets, safety, quality, and federal documentation requirements.

The Sr. PM integrates all project management knowledge areas (scope, cost, time, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholder management) so the project functions as a cohesive whole. This position serves as a primary point of contact with clients and agencies and effectively leads teams of scientists, engineers, procurement specialists, subcontractors, field personnel, and other stakeholders to meet CAPE’s financial and performance goals.

This role is onsite at active project locations. Not a remote role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead onsite project execution to deliver scope safely, on schedule, and within budget; develop the execution approach, staffing plan, and phased work plan based on scope and risk.
Build and run the Project Management Plan (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholders) and keep plans/baselines current as changes occur.
Control scope using WBS/work packages; manage contract requirements, modifications, and change orders, including impact analysis and timely approvals.
Develop and maintain the integrated schedule (near-term planning through milestones); drive weekly/monthly reporting, corrective actions, and a monthly performance analysis/forecast.
Own project financial performance, cost control, forecasting (ETC/EAC), variance analysis, and recovery plans; identify cost drivers and correct excessive-cost items.
Embed safety and quality into planning and field execution; ensure Safety Plans are in place and followed; maintain incident reporting and a zero-incident culture.
Manage procurement and subcontractors, define and negotiate scopes, oversee performance and invoices, and ensure submittals and progress payments are processed accurately and on time.
Serve as primary client/agency interface (USACE/USEPA as applicable); communicate progress, risks, and issues to stakeholders and executive management; resolve disputes professionally and promptly.
Supervise and lead project staff in accordance with company policies and applicable laws; perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills, Knowledge & Tools

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical procedures, engineering drawings/specifications, and applicable government regulations (including FAR familiarity).
Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to write clear reports/correspondence and confidently present project status, risks, and decisions to stakeholders.
Persuasive communicator with effective negotiation skills; able to develop strong working relationships with executive management, clients, and subcontractors.
Primavera P6 scheduling experience (required/strongly preferred).

Salary

Up to $160,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Travel

50 % on average

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications (Project Manager II) – bachelor’s degree in engineering/science or construction management required. Must have at least three (3) years of progressively responsible related field experience and task management, and two (2) years of onsite Quality Control experience supporting environmental and/or infrastructure work. Must demonstrate a firm grasp of the key project management knowledge areas (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, risk, procurement, communications, stakeholders) as determined by management review.
Senior-Level Requirements (in addition to the above) – Minimum ten (10) years of successful project management experience with emphasis on cost, schedule, communications, and resource management on construction and/or environmental remediation projects. Must have a professional certification (PMP, PE, or PG) and a proven track record delivering complex work (including successfully managing at least two (2) projects over $5M). Must have (or be able to obtain) required field credentials including OSHA 30-Hour Construction and 40-hour HAZWOPER with current refreshers.
Tools / Scheduling – Proficient in Microsoft Office and Windows-based systems; strong ability to develop and maintain project schedules. Primavera P6 experience required (or strongly preferred, depending on your HR “required vs preferred” structure).

Preferred Qualifications

Field experience in construction or environmental projects.

Not the production network - the infrastructure that lets engineers monitor, manage, control, and recover everything else. Out-of-band connectivity, facility networks, disaster recovery backbone, device management networks, and the security layer that protects them all. When something goes wrong in a data centre, these are the systems that make recovery possible.

If you have managed large-scale infrastructure network deployments, understand the difference between a plan of record and what actually happens on site, and know how to hold vendors and partners accountable without burning the relationship, this role is built for you.

What you will own

Own end-to-end programme delivery across network deployments globally. New builds, retrofits, and end-of-life hardware replacements. You set the programme plan, define milestones, manage the critical path, and hold every stakeholder accountable to it.
Translate strategic roadmaps into executable delivery plans. You will lead H1 and H2 planning cycles and turn a twelve-month supply execution plan into a weekly operating reality across vendors, engineers, and operations teams.
Drive hardware and supply chain accountability. You will ensure BOMs are ordered correctly and on time, track hardware deliveries to site, manage Hardware Need-By Dates across multiple internal teams, and identify long-lead procurement risks before they become programme blockers.
Manage cross-functional dependencies across network engineering, supply chain, security, and operations. You will not wait for problems to surface. You will find them early, escalate fast, and drive resolution.

Proven programme management rigour in a complex infrastructure environment. You have managed multi-workstream programmes with hard deadlines, held vendors and engineering teams accountable, and made decisions under pressure when ambiguity was high and the schedule could not slip.
Hands-on experience managing infrastructure network deployments in a data centre or mission-critical environment. You understand what it takes to get management and facility network infrastructure from design through commissioning and operational handoff. Technical fluency across management and operational network infrastructure. Vendor and contractor accountability. You have managed multi-vendor delivery environments where no single team owns the entire critical path. You know how to keep external partners aligned, escalate when needed, and maintain the relationship through difficult conversations.

Prior experience managing infrastructure network deployments inside a hyperscaler or large-scale data centre environment.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. The organization's mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. The initial focus was on solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The administrative work – credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation – is complex. Automation has been implemented to address this.

The organization is going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on the software, serving over 1 million patients. The goal is to build the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagine the experience of finding a therapist, and invest in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. This is more than just a billing layer; it is becoming the platform where care actually happens.

This is a Series D organization with significant funding, looking for exceptional people to help achieve this mission. The aim is for time spent here to be the most meaningful experience of one's career. Joining this team means helping to change mental healthcare for the better.

As the organization works to build a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access, it is facing unique operational challenges and opportunities that come with growing and scaling at an unparalleled rate. The boundaries of the existing healthcare system are being pushed to fulfill the promise to providers, patients, and payers to create access to high-quality providers across the nation. To achieve this, a world-class operations team is being built to enable efficiency, growth, and quality. As a member of this team, there will be an opportunity to have a material impact on the trajectory of the organization and help define a function core to the livelihood of the business and the impact delivered for partners and clients.

As a Business Operations Manager, the individual will lead high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that span teams and pods. This role will operate as a thought partner to Product, Data, and Operations leaders – helping shape objectives, influence priorities, and translate complex insights into actionable plans. In addition to owning critical operational workflows, the individual will design scalable systems, mentor team members, and drive initiatives that create durable, measurable impact across the organization. This role requires strong judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to drive alignment and execution across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Design and build foundations for a variety of 0-1 initiatives within the Business Operations function.
Collaborate cross-functionally to build, execute, monitor, and implement scalable products and processes that enable the organization to deliver on core business challenges.
Assess and analyze data to develop and determine strategies for accelerating progress, proactively identify areas for improvement, and deliver on roadmap priorities and team OKRs.
Build and manage a growing team to achieve these objectives.

Required Qualifications

7+ years of experience in operational roles at high-growth companies, with some background in consulting or finance, business operations preferred but not required.
Data is a first language; enjoyment and skill in digging through complex data to solve ambiguous problems.
Thrives in the unknown, seeking out opportunities to dive into unfamiliar challenges, drive towards outcomes, and shape strategy.
Operationally excellent, able to manage a large volume of moving pieces without breaking a sweat.
A collaborator that proactively partners across teams while holding teams accountable for business results.
Seeks an environment that fosters individual growth through open feedback and high autonomy.
Motivated by the opportunity to make an impact on one of the generation's defining problems: affordable mental healthcare.

The expected base pay range for this position is $121,600 - $190,000. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for an equity grant, depending on the position and level.

The organization is committed to offering a comprehensive and competitive total rewards package, including robust health and wellness benefits, retirement savings, and meaningful ownership opportunities through equity. Build like a founder. Ship like Spartan.

Our clients are startups in a race: an MVP in 30 days, one demo away from a funding round. We’re looking for a Technical PM to run that race and keep every piece on track.
We don’t act like vendors. We embed. Our teams sit inside startups backed by YC, Pear VC, BlingCap, a16z, and Techstars, working beside founders and engineers from Stanford, MIT, Yale, Google, Amazon, and Uber. Together we ship those MVPs and scale the systems behind them to millions of users and billions of requests.
This isn’t a ticket-pushing PM role. You are the person a US founder calls when they need the truth about their product. You own scope, timeline, quality, and the client relationship. The engineers build. You make sure the right thing ships, on time, and the client knows exactly where things stand. And the Technical in the title is real: you read the architecture, question the estimates, and hold your own in an engineering discussion.
70% of our portfolio is LLM-powered. You’ll scope AI features, plan around model risk, and use Cursor and Claude yourself to write specs and plans faster.

Who Thrives at Spartan
Not every environment fits everyone, so here’s an honest picture of the teammate we’re looking for.
You’ll thrive here if:
You own the outcome: scope, timeline, quality, and the relationship.
You’re technical enough that engineers can’t hand-wave you, and clear enough that founders never feel lost.
You can tell a founder no, with a reason and a plan.
You wear many hats without being asked: PM today, BA tomorrow, QA on release day.
You step into an at-risk project and bring it back to green.

Some weeks will stretch you. That’s the job. But you’ll never carry it alone. A critical client release or a hard founder conversation? The team is right there with you. We push each other hard because we care how far each of us can go. We win together. We lose together. Nobody gets left behind.
One last thing. We’re not filling seats. We’re looking for teammates for the battles ahead. If you read all this and something in you said yes, trust that feeling and apply. We respect people who back themselves. Every Spartan here started with that same yes.

What You’ll Do
Own delivery of client engagements end to end: scope, estimate, timeline, quality.
Be the daily voice to US startup founders. Run async standups, write sharp status updates, deliver bad news early and with a plan.
Turn vague founder ideas into PRDs and RFCs the team can ship in 30 days.
Scope AI features with clear eyes: what the model can do today, what needs a spike, and how to demo it honestly.
Plan AI work differently: prototype first, define evals early, budget for iteration.
Read the tech. Challenge estimates. Discuss architecture trade-offs with your Team Lead, then explain them to the founder in business language.
Track project health (Green / Yellow / Red), raise risks before they blow up, escalate with options, not problems.
Run the delivery process: sprints, code review SLAs, release plans, demos.
Support pre-sales: feasibility checks and estimates for new deals.
Wear whatever hat the project needs to win.

What We’re Looking For
Fluent English, spoken and written. You talk to US founders every day.
An engineering background. You’ve written production code, or worked close enough to it that a padded estimate can’t get past you.
3+ years running software delivery at an agency, consulting firm, or startup. That means you owned the projects, not just attended the standups.
You’ve told a client something they didn’t want to hear, and kept the contract.
You can persuade a non-technical founder to invest two sprints in tech debt, in their language, not jargon.
You work AI-native: Cursor, Claude, Codex. You use AI to plan, write, and move faster.
An owner’s mindset. You own outcomes, not tickets.

Nice to Have
Experience shipping LLM-powered products.
Experience with US or other Western clients.
Hands-on backend or frontend experience you can still use in a pinch.

Tools We Use
Notion · Slack · Linear · Jira · GitHub · Figma Cursor · Claude · Codex

Career Growth
Work directly with founders from YC, Stanford, MIT, Yale, Google, Amazon, Uber, and more.
Exposure to how AI products get scoped, built, and launched across many startup domains.
Transparent career path and mentorship from engineers who’ve taken 3 companies to IPO.
Every project feels like its own mini-startup.

Why Spartan
50+ MVPs launched, 3 IPOs, $100M+ raised by the startups we build with.
95% engineer retention. People stay because the work is worth staying for.
You take products zero to one. From a founder’s idea to a live launch in weeks. Most PMs get that chance once in a career. Here it’s the job.
Your work is visible. The product you run this month is in a founder’s investor demo next month.
No layers, no bureaucracy. You talk to the decision-maker directly, and decisions land in hours, not weeks.
Every project is a new market, a new team, a new problem. One year here teaches what three years elsewhere would.
You’ll never just take tickets. You’ll own problems, ship fast, and grow with the founders we partner with.

Benefits & Perks

Summary Of Job Description

The Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) assists CAPE in achieving strategic and business objectives by leading project management processes (initiation, planning, executing, monitoring/controlling, and closing) for projects across New Jersey. This Sr. PM role is responsible for both construction and environmental remediation delivery and must be capable of managing field execution, subcontractors, schedules, budgets, safety, quality, and federal documentation requirements.

The Sr. PM integrates all project management knowledge areas (scope, cost, time, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholder management) so the project functions as a cohesive whole. This position serves as a primary point of contact with clients and agencies and effectively leads teams of scientists, engineers, procurement specialists, subcontractors, field personnel, and other stakeholders to meet CAPE’s financial and performance goals.

This role is onsite at active project locations. Not a remote role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead onsite project execution to deliver scope safely, on schedule, and within budget; develop the execution approach, staffing plan, and phased work plan based on scope and risk.
Build and run the Project Management Plan (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholders) and keep plans/baselines current as changes occur.
Control scope using WBS/work packages; manage contract requirements, modifications, and change orders, including impact analysis and timely approvals.
Develop and maintain the integrated schedule (near-term planning through milestones); drive weekly/monthly reporting, corrective actions, and a monthly performance analysis/forecast.
Own project financial performance, cost control, forecasting (ETC/EAC), variance analysis, and recovery plans; identify cost drivers and correct excessive-cost items.
Embed safety and quality into planning and field execution; ensure Safety Plans are in place and followed; maintain incident reporting and a zero-incident culture.
Manage procurement and subcontractors, define and negotiate scopes, oversee performance and invoices, and ensure submittals and progress payments are processed accurately and on time.
Serve as primary client/agency interface (USACE/USEPA as applicable); communicate progress, risks, and issues to stakeholders and executive management; resolve disputes professionally and promptly.
Supervise and lead project staff in accordance with company policies and applicable laws; perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills, Knowledge & Tools

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical procedures, engineering drawings/specifications, and applicable government regulations (including FAR familiarity).
Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to write clear reports/correspondence and confidently present project status, risks, and decisions to stakeholders.
Persuasive communicator with effective negotiation skills; able to develop strong working relationships with executive management, clients, and subcontractors.
Primavera P6 scheduling experience (required/strongly preferred).

Salary

Up to $160,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Travel

50 % on average

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications (Project Manager II) – bachelor’s degree in engineering/science or construction management required. Must have at least three (3) years of progressively responsible related field experience and task management, and two (2) years of onsite Quality Control experience supporting environmental and/or infrastructure work. Must demonstrate a firm grasp of the key project management knowledge areas (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, risk, procurement, communications, stakeholders) as determined by management review.
Senior-Level Requirements (in addition to the above) – Minimum ten (10) years of successful project management experience with emphasis on cost, schedule, communications, and resource management on construction and/or environmental remediation projects. Must have a professional certification (PMP, PE, or PG) and a proven track record delivering complex work (including successfully managing at least two (2) projects over $5M). Must have (or be able to obtain) required field credentials including OSHA 30-Hour Construction and 40-hour HAZWOPER with current refreshers.
Tools / Scheduling – Proficient in Microsoft Office and Windows-based systems; strong ability to develop and maintain project schedules. Primavera P6 experience required (or strongly preferred, depending on your HR “required vs preferred” structure).

Preferred Qualifications

Field experience in construction or environmental projects.

WHY CAPE?

For 35 years, CAPE has delivered construction and environmental remediation solutions to governmental and private organizations nationwide. As a $100 M small business, we have Nationwide contracts with the USACE, USN and USAF totaling over $20 B in prime contract capacity. As a top 3 SB in our industry, our $12 B portfolio also includes unrestricted contracts where we compete against large businesses for task order awards. Most recently in the unrestricted area, CAPE won a $30 M + groundwater treatment plant construction project for the USACE in New Jersey. We routinely partner with other small and large businesses to provide better responsiveness in support of achieving our clients’ goals.

Our projects are high-profile environmental remediation projects involving cleanup of contaminated soil, groundwater, and sediment. The culture of our company is one of working together to achieve our clients’ objectives, company goals and employee’s professional goals and is succinctly and accurately defined as “We, Not Me” behavior. To ensure long-term, sustainable growth, we tailor our 3-year vision to be ahead of our industry in delivering our projects, align with our clients and team partners to improve our existing market share and develop new services to support smart growth.

CAPE offers competitive benefits including Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, life insurance, Vanguard retirement savings plan including both traditional and Roth 401(k) with up to 4% match and lowest in class fees, health savings account (HSA) with investment option, flexible spending account (FSA), paid annual leave, paid maternity/paternity leave, and tuition reimbursement. CAPE also offers staff several other voluntary benefits options, as well as the option to work from home.

Technical Program Manager | Infrastructure Network Engineering | Fully Remote, United States

A global organisation is looking for a Technical Program Manager to own the end-to-end delivery of infrastructure network programmes across one of the most operationally critical environments in the world.

You will run deployment and retrofit programmes from initial planning through to handoff, coordinating across network engineering, supply chain, and operations teams to ensure management and facility network infrastructure lands on time, on spec, and ready to operate.
The programmes you will own are the backbone of data centre resilience.

Not the production network - the infrastructure that lets engineers monitor, manage, control, and recover everything else. Out-of-band connectivity, facility networks, disaster recovery backbone, device management networks, and the security layer that protects them all. When something goes wrong in a data centre, these are the systems that make recovery possible.

If you have managed large-scale infrastructure network deployments, understand the difference between a plan of record and what actually happens on site, and know how to hold vendors and partners accountable without burning the relationship, this role is built for you.

What you will own

Own end-to-end programme delivery across network deployments globally. New builds, retrofits, and end-of-life hardware replacements. You set the programme plan, define milestones, manage the critical path, and hold every stakeholder accountable to it.
Translate strategic roadmaps into executable delivery plans. You will lead H1 and H2 planning cycles and turn a twelve-month supply execution plan into a weekly operating reality across vendors, engineers, and operations teams.
Drive hardware and supply chain accountability. You will ensure BOMs are ordered correctly and on time, track hardware deliveries to site, manage Hardware Need-By Dates across multiple internal teams, and identify long-lead procurement risks before they become programme blockers.
Manage cross-functional dependencies across network engineering, supply chain, security, and operations. You will not wait for problems to surface. You will find them early, escalate fast, and drive resolution.
Establish and maintain programme governance. Programme trackers, status decks, risk registers, executive reporting, and lessons learned reviews are yours. Leadership should never be surprised by what is happening in your programme.

What you need

Proven programme management rigour in a complex infrastructure environment. You have managed multi-workstream programmes with hard deadlines, held vendors and engineering teams accountable, and made decisions under pressure when ambiguity was high and the schedule could not slip.
Hands-on experience managing infrastructure network deployments in a data centre or mission-critical environment. You understand what it takes to get management and facility network infrastructure from design through commissioning and operational handoff. You know what breaks, why it breaks, and how to prevent it.
Technical fluency across management and operational network infrastructure. You do not need to be a network engineer but you need to hold your own in conversations about out-of-band connectivity, facility networks, device management, and DR backbone architecture. You ask the right questions and recognise when the answers do not add up.
Hardware and BOM management experience. You have managed equipment procurement at scale - tracking lead times, coordinating deliveries, and ensuring the right hardware is on site when the programme needs it. End-of-life and end-of-support retrofit experience is a strong plus.
Vendor and contractor accountability. You have managed multi-vendor delivery environments where no single team owns the entire critical path. You know how to keep external partners aligned, escalate when needed, and maintain the relationship through difficult conversations.
Risk identification and programme health management. You maintain a live risk register, proactively surface issues to leadership, and run lessons learned reviews that actually change how the next programme runs.

What will set you apart

Prior experience managing infrastructure network deployments inside a hyperscaler or large-scale data centre environment.
Familiarity with out-of-band management networks, facility systems including power and environmental monitoring, disaster recovery backbone networking, or PON technology in a data centre context.
Experience managing the full hardware lifecycle from BOM generation and procurement through delivery, staging, installation, and decommissioning including end-of-life replacement programmes.
Background in supply chain coordination or capacity planning for infrastructure programmes where long-lead hardware is on the critical path.
Experience building and running a Tactical Plan of Record or equivalent twelve-month supply execution planning process.
Phased rollout experience across new build, retrofit, and end-of-life replacement programme types simultaneously across multiple global sites.
